requirement_text.REQ-425:
MOB-6 in docs/mobile/requirements.md (build-order M6; depends on M2). Built BEFORE MOB-4 (REQ-426..428) -- see the S9 header: the renderers' six states classify this requirement's ApiError. SECURITY-REVIEWER gate (refresh-token handling, token clearing).

Hardens lib/api/api_client.dart (created by REQ-421) into the single client:
1. Attach the active tenant's bearer token (REQ-422's iss check).
2. On 401: exactly one silent refresh via flutter_appauth's token refresh, then exactly one retry of the original request; concurrent 401s share one in-flight refresh. On refresh failure: clear the tenant's tokens (REQ-422 store) and route to login.
3. Exponential backoff on 5xx for idempotent methods only (GET), bounded attempts; POST is not auto-retried (no duplicate task completion).
4. Normalise every failure to a sealed ApiError type before it leaves lib/api/: at minimum network-unavailable, unauthorized, forbidden (403), not-found, module-not-available (a 404 on any /api/v1/modules/<id>/ path -- architecture.md §6: absence is 404, not 403, and must not render as a generic not-found), backpressure (429, carrying the Retry-After seconds -- the backend emits 429 from lib/letflow/plugs/admission.ex and lib/letflow/plugs/public_read_rate_limit.ex), validation (422 with RFC 9457 field errors), conflict (409), server (5xx after retries).
5. A static guard (apps/mobile/test/guards/), the counterpart of the SPA's raw-fetch-outside-client guard in web/tests/guards/: no file outside lib/api/ imports package:dio or package:http or uses dart:io HttpClient; with a self-test.

task.description:
Step 2d of WF-02 for REQ-425. Read git diff main...HEAD -- apps/mobile/ (15 files, +1392/-142 as of the initial implementation, plus rework 1/2's cross-tenant-race fixes on top). This code went through 3 SECURITY-REVIEWER cycles finding and closing 2 real cross-tenant token races (token-write-time, then retry-dispatch-time) -- read handoffs/WF02-REQ425-20260929/step-02c-security-reviewer-recheck2.json's gate_history for that history rather than having it restated here.

Run the standard REVIEWER procedure per .claude/agents/reviewer.md's four questions (idiomatic vs. crutch, supervision integrity -- N/A for mobile/Dart, but check for equivalent structural soundness in the async coordination pattern, type-safety gaps, scope creep) and against docs/anti-patterns.md. Specific things worth your judgment given this run's own history: (1) is the final _RefreshCoordinator/_bearerInterceptor design (now patched twice under security pressure) still a coherent, maintainable mechanism, or has it accumulated patch-on-patch complexity that should be restructured before merge? (2) MOBILE-DEV's original implementation disclosed 3 deviations from the PASSed design (clientId sourcing added to ActiveRealmHolder, a new `on ForbiddenError` catch in navigation_bootstrap.dart, Riverpod provider type-annotation changes) -- SECURITY-REVIEWER already cleared these for security; check them for idiom/scope-creep now (do they belong in this requirement's scope, or should any have been routed elsewhere?). (3) Check for scope creep generally -- this requirement's own acceptance criteria are the boundary, not anything else touched incidentally. FAIL if a genuine crutch, structural unsoundness, or scope creep is found; otherwise PASS with any non-blocking notes recorded.
acceptance_criteria: a test where the fake server returns 401 once then 200 asserts exactly one refresh call and exactly one retry, and that two concurrent requests both receiving 401 trigger one refresh total
a test where refresh fails asserts the tenant's tokens are deleted from the secure store and the router is at the login route

a test asserts a GET receiving 503 twice then 200 succeeds with increasing delays between attempts (fake clock), a GET receiving 503 on every attempt stops after the maximum attempt count declared as a named constant in lib/api/ and surfaces ApiError server (the test asserts the exact number of requests sent), and a POST receiving 503 is not retried

a test per ApiError variant asserts the mapping from status code/exception, including 404 on /api/v1/modules/exam/x -> module-not-available, 404 elsewhere -> not-found, and 429 with 'Retry-After: 7' -> backpressure(7 seconds)
a test asserts no DioException or SocketException escapes lib/api/ -- the public client API returns or throws only ApiError
the single-client guard fails its self-test fixture (a file under lib/features/ importing package:dio) and passes on the real tree
cd apps/mobile && flutter analyze && flutter test pass, real output quoted, and SECURITY-REVIEWER signs off before merge

result.summary:
First-hand read of git diff main...HEAD -- apps/mobile/ (api_client.dart, api_error.dart, auth.dart, navigation_bootstrap.dart, api.dart, single_api_client_guard_test.dart, api_client_hardening_test.dart, plus fakes). Judged against the four REVIEWER questions and the three specific calls in this handoff's task.

(1) _RefreshCoordinator/_bearerInterceptor coherence after 2 security reworks: PASS, not a patch-on-patch mess. The mechanism has exactly three re-check points, each with a distinct, non-overlapping reason documented at its definition: _doRefresh's pre-persist re-check (rework 1, token-write-time), _handleUnauthorized's pre-fetch re-check (original design), and _bearerInterceptor's own token-attach-time re-check (rework 2, retry-dispatch-time -- closes the real dio 5.11.1 event-loop-turn window the other two cannot see). These are not three redundant patches over the same hole; each closes a genuinely different window in the same async sequence, and the doc comments on _kIssuedForRealmKey and _RefreshOutcome.aborted explain why the aborted/failed distinction exists (a switch-away is not this tenant's failure to report). The design stayed a single coordinator + single interceptor pair throughout -- no new class or abstraction layer was added to paper over the races; each rework tightened an existing check site. This is what correct iteration under a security gate should look like, not scope/structure decay. One maintainability note (non-blocking): the three re-check sites' invariant ("only ever trust a realm value captured before the point in question, never re-read after") is now load-bearing across three separate functions with no single named helper or assertion tying them together -- worth a comment audit or a small shared helper if a fourth window is ever found, but not a defect today; the existing regression tests (rework 1 and rework 2 groups in api_client_hardening_test.dart) pin the current behavior.

(2) MOBILE-DEV's 3 disclosed deviations, judged for idiom/scope (security already cleared): (a) ActiveRealmHolder.clientId -- in scope; the refresh_token grant genuinely needs it alongside currentRealmUrl, and it is lifecycle-matched to currentRealmUrl everywhere (bootstrap, switchTenant, logout all null both together) -- no partial-state risk introduced. (b) navigation_bootstrap.dart's new `on ForbiddenError` catch -- in scope and in fact required, not incidental: REQ-425 changes ApiClient.get's contract from 'returns a Response for any status' to 'throws ApiError for non-2xx', which necessarily invalidates the old `else if (status == 403)` branch on a Response that a hardened get() no longer returns for a 403. Not fixing this would have silently broken the existing 'membership check not applicable, proceed to modules' behavior. The old status==403 branch is correctly kept as a defensive fallback for fakes, with a comment explaining why it's now believed unreachable against the real client. (c) Riverpod provider explicit type annotations (`Provider<ApiClient>`, `ChangeNotifierProvider<BootstrapController>`) -- trivial, no behavior change, not scope creep. None of the three should have been routed elsewhere; all three are direct, unavoidable consequences of this requirement's own contract change to ApiClient.get/post.

(3) General scope creep: none found. RedactingLogInterceptor is REQ-422 infrastructure explicitly left unregistered by that requirement for REQ-425 to adopt -- adopting it here (registered in ApiClient.create, not forTesting) is using existing infrastructure for its intended purpose, not building ahead of need. classifyError's catch-all (unmapped status -> ServerError) is honestly flagged in its own comment as OQ-1 for REVIEWER rather than silently decided -- accepted as reasonable pending a real unmapped-status case; not a defect.

Idiomatic vs. crutch: sound. The refresh/retry logic is deliberately implemented as method-body logic (_sendWithBackoff/_handleUnauthorized) rather than a Dio onError interceptor, with the reasoning given inline (validateStatus accepts everything, so onError would never fire) -- this is the correct call for Dio's request model, not a hand-rolled substitute for something the framework already does. Async coordination (Dart's equivalent of supervision/isolation here) is sound: _RefreshCoordinator's single nullable in-flight Future is the idiomatic Dart coalescing pattern (no locks/mutexes needed in a single-isolate event loop), and every one of the three race-window fixes is backed by a named regression test group, not just a comment claiming correctness.

Type-safety: ApiError is a Dart 3 sealed class (exhaustiveness-checked), which is exactly the right tool here and already used -- no gap to file. classifyError's OQ-1 catch-all is a judgment call already surfaced, not a hidden gap.

docs/anti-patterns.md: no Dart/Flutter/mobile entries exist yet to check against; nothing in this diff suggests a new entry is warranted.

Verdict: PASS. No crutch, no structural unsoundness, no scope creep. Non-blocking note recorded above (three-site re-check invariant could use a shared helper/assertion if touched again).
